scope: Observed authenticated Chrome UI on actual Render Linux deployment, using two short authored mathematics fixtures. Not synthetic transport, not a student pilot or a general model accuracy benchmark.
checks: Actual Google OAuth sign-in completed after a fresh retry; an earlier stale attempt returned AccessDenied.
Uploaded a valid authored two-page Vietnamese PDF; actual Linux document worker extracted 482 characters with page locations.
Indexed the authored text fixture (562 characters, five chunks) and the PDF fixture (two chunks), each revision1.
After separate external-AI consent, two real document embedding calls succeeded; both indexed documents displayed lexical plus semantic status.
A real hybrid query returned six excerpts from both documents, including the PDF page1 and page2 locations.
A tutor session selected both indexed documents and separate semantic-query consent. The source snapshot remained fixed across four tutor turns.
Observed server hint progress 0 to1 to2 to3; full solution stayed locked before3 valid hints and became available after3.
After the intentionally wrong learner result x=6, the tutor identified the division mistake and asked the learner to recompute or substitute, without supplying the final numeric answer in that hint.
Requested the full solution after the gate: x=5, with 3x=15, division by nonzero3 and substitution 3*5-6=9.
Citations displayed exact authored PDF quotes on pages1/2 and authored text paragraphs. Opened page2 quote matched the supplied text.
limits: One short exercise and two tiny authored sources cannot establish general educational accuracy or production capacity.

The first tutor question contained free prose around the equation. The deliberately strict independent equation parser marked this case not supported; UI did not show a false verified badge. Mathematical answer was manually checked separately.
Hint2/3 repeated some wording between feedback and hint; pedagogy remains partial and has no independent teacher review.
